terms.comment: Traupman’s word (feminine ēditrīx), from ēdere, to bring out a book, which is classical (see launch). Classically ēditor is rare and late: one who gives games (Lewis & Short). The editor of a text or a paper is another word (see editor).

terms.gloss: a bookseller (who had copies made and sold them)
evidence: M-O s.v. publisher: bibliopōlium, a publishing house
terms.comment: Greek βιβλιοπώλης. In Rome the bookseller had an author’s work copied and sold it,, and was what a publisher is now. Post-Augustan.

sources: Lewis & Short: editor · Lewis & Short: bibliopola
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 169, checked against the searchable text of the book. Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. publisher, publishing house.
